message.content: In lions, one of the most noticeable dominant traits is the **presence of a mane in adult males**. The gene that controls mane development is inherited in a dominant fashion: if a male lion inherits the dominant allele (often referred to as “M” for mane), it will develop a mane, whereas the recessive allele (“m”) results in a maneless phenotype. This dominant trait is why most male lions have a mane, while females (who are typically homozygous recessive, “mm”) do not.
